--- page 1 ---
Chapter 1
Tidal gardens form where a shallow shelf of rock holds seawater between tides.
Small pools warm quickly in the sun, and their chemistry shifts within a few hours.
Animals that live there must tolerate heat, salt and sudden rain.
--- page 2 ---
Chapter 2
The library also lends databases such as ProQuest to its members.
Copyright law differs between countries, and readers should check the rules that apply to them.
The next chapter turns to the algae that colour the upper shore.
--- page 3 ---
Chapter 3
Green algae dominate the high pools, where light is strong and grazers are few.
Lower down, red algae spread beneath the shade of larger brown weeds.
Each band of colour marks a different balance of light and wave action.
